body:
Current Central Cargo memory budget (integration owner Opus2 enforces; revised rules from 2026-11-05 23:11Z; retained after Engram::Fable full second reading 2026-11-09 mailbox-message-aa30dc95-2e93-42d2-862f-65e4a7e7cd4a): one Cargo job at a time, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4. A -j4 start requires FreeVirtualMemory >=26 GB (measured peak plus 8 GB reserve). A start with 16–26 GB uses -j2; do not start below16 GB. Owner stops its own run below6 GB and records a resource stop, not a test result. More specific current coordinator windows/holds still apply. The -j2 estimate remains subject to measurement.

Measurement provenance: Opus2 observed Sol-license test-9e0b6762 (-j4 compile plus336 tests/threads4): FreeVirtual34.7GB at start,17.07GB minimum,35.1GB after, about17.6GB peak commit; first75s sampled coarsely. Sampler .logs/central-freevirtual-8111.log. This superseded the earlier22GB -j4 line in revision1–2; those historical revisions remain accessible.

Greg's word relayed by Engram::Asistant #445, verbatim: «To chyba jest max teraz co mamy.» The old associated paged-pool task w-cf039ab7b131 is cancelled; this does not end the still-current safety rule. Its retirement target is cleared rather than treating the cancelled investigation as expiry of the rule.

REVISION 2026-11-10 05:12Z (Opus2, approved by Fable2 #5273): -j2 compiles on Central may START at a 20.0 GiB raw FreeVirtualMemory floor. Read the raw KiB value; don't round. Conditions: one Cargo job at a time, and no other rustc running. Background: after the 05:02Z restart, Central's free virtual memory stayed at 19-22 GiB, and the stricter 22 GiB hold we had been applying blocked the queued -j2 Windows-only and live jobs. 20 GiB is inside this memory's own rule: a start at 16-26 GB uses -j2, and nothing starts below 16 GB. So this loosens only the extra hold, not the agreed budget; Engram::Fable has re-read it. Unchanged: -j4 needs ≥ 26 GB; RUST_TEST_THREADS=4; a running job stops itself below 6 GB and records a resource stop; pair or evaluator spawns need FV ≥ 16 GB with no rustc above about 5 GB; and the next compile is held until a granted pair's SPAWN line.

REVISION 2026-11-10 05:16Z (Opus2, at Engram::Fable's request in TermAl mailbox 28ccc255 #508): Engram's standing author-Clippy rule (#482) also uses the 20.0 GiB RAW floor. Its conditions: one Engram author at a time, no rustc and no cargo on the shared target dir at start, -j 2, START and END to Opus2, a stop at about 10 minutes, and a self-stop below 6 GB. Added condition, after the 03:36Z collision: a #482 run may start only when no NAMED Central GO is outstanding, meaning granted with no END yet. Named GOs always go first.

REVISION 2026-11-11 (Opus2; concurred by Fable2 TermAl mailbox 4daa5b87 #5437, by Engram::Fable mailbox 28ccc255 #578, and for the amended (3) by Fable2 #5441):
Measurement: edfd's -j 2 `cargo test --bin termal` run test-8f9345d2 (6c533f9d, 457 tests) STARTed at 22980080 KiB raw FreeVirtualMemory. During its link, one rustc reached about 17.2 GB private, and FV fell to 3463648 KiB at 01:53:14Z. Sol-c593's read-only reviewer pair was running at the same time. The host's own termal used about 4.2 GB. Nothing was killed, and the run passed.
Rules from now on:
(1) A -j 2 build that links the termal binary or its test binary (cargo test, clippy or build of --bin termal) STARTs only under one of two conditions:
  (a) raw FV >= 25165824 KiB (24 GiB); or
  (b) raw FV >= 20971520 KiB (20 GiB), and no reviewer pair, evaluator or other spawned agent session starts on Central from its START to its END. Opus2 holds such spawns while it runs.
(2) A pair or evaluator spawn while a granted cargo job runs needs both of these: the job STARTed under (1a), and FV >= 16 GiB with no rustc above about 5 GB at the spawn. Otherwise the spawn waits for END+RELEASE.
(3) Large author test builds go to DL560's author slot when it is free or would start sooner than Central. These are a --bin termal test compile, or an Engram --lib test or Clippy build. Central keeps Windows-only steps and runs that need Central itself. An Engram test or Clippy build whose purpose is Windows coverage (Windows-only code, or a Windows gate or a check before one) counts as a Windows-only step.
(4) "Stops its own run below 6 GB" is replaced, because no process is killed (Engram w-fa603145720d) and the TermAl launcher has no stop subcommand. Below 6 GB, the run's monitor reports to Opus2 and the run finishes. The episode is recorded as a resource incident, not a test result. A monitor has no kill path at all.
Unchanged: one cargo job at a time; RUST_TEST_THREADS=4; -j 4 needs >= 26 GB; nothing starts below 16 GB; Engram's #482 author-Clippy rule, which now also follows (1) when it links the termal binary.
